title: Big Ideas 2026 (Parts 1-3)
edition_framing: Each idea is what a16z partners expect builders to tackle in 2026.

entries.label: Startups tame the chaos of multimodal data
entries.quote: That’s why untangling unstructured data becomes a generational opportunity.
entries.subject: Multimodal unstructured enterprise data
entries.author: Jennifer Li

entries.label: AI revives cybersecurity hiring
entries.quote: In 2026, AI will break this cycle and close this hiring gap by automating much of this repetitive and redundant work for cybersecurity teams.
entries.subject: AI automation in cybersecurity
entries.author: Joel de la Garza

entries.label: Agent-native infrastructure becomes table stakes
entries.quote: In 2026, the biggest infrastructure shock won’t come from outside companies, but from within.
entries.subject: Agent-native infrastructure
entries.author: Malika Aubakirova

entries.label: Creative tools go multimodal
entries.quote: Content creation is one of the killer use cases of AI, and I expect we’ll see multiple successful products across use cases and types of customers from meme makers to Hollywood directors.
entries.subject: Multimodal AI creative tools
entries.author: Justine Moore

entries.label: The AI-native data stack continues to evolve
entries.quote: While the ecosystem feels notably more mature, we’re still in the early days of a truly AI-native data architecture.
entries.subject: AI-native data stack
entries.author: Jason Cui

entries.label: The year we step inside video
entries.quote: In 2026, video stops behaving like something we passively watch and starts feeling like a place we can actually step into.
entries.subject: Interactive generative video (world models)
entries.author: Yoko Li

entries.label: Systems of record lose ground
entries.quote: In 2026, the real disruption in enterprise software is that the system of record will finally start to lose primacy.
entries.subject: Enterprise systems of record
entries.author: Sarah Wang

entries.label: Vertical AI evolves from information retrieval and reasoning to multiplayer
entries.quote: 2026 unlocks multiplayer mode.
entries.subject: Multiplayer vertical AI agents
entries.author: Alex Immerman

entries.label: Creating for agents, not humans
entries.quote: In 2026, people will start interfacing with the web through their agents.
entries.subject: AI agents as web users
entries.author: Stephenie Zhang

entries.label: The end of the screen time KPI in AI applications
entries.quote: As we move to a future based on outcome-based pricing that perfectly aligns incentives between vendors and users, we’ll first move away from screen time reporting.
entries.subject: Outcome-based metrics for AI applications
entries.author: Santiago Rodriguez

entries.label: Healthy MAUs
entries.quote: In 2026, a new healthcare customer segment will take center stage: the “healthy MAUs.”
entries.subject: Consumer preventive healthcare ("healthy MAUs")
entries.author: Julie Yoo

entries.label: World models take the spotlight in storytelling
entries.quote: In 2026, AI-powered world models will revolutionize storytelling through interactive virtual worlds and digital economies.
entries.subject: World models for interactive storytelling
entries.author: Jonathan Lai

entries.label: “The year of me”
entries.quote: 2026 will become “the year of me”: the moment when products stop being mass-produced and start being made for you.
entries.subject: AI personalization of products
entries.author: Joshua Lu

entries.label: The first AI-native university
entries.quote: In 2026, I expect we’ll see the birth of the first AI-native university, an institution built from the ground up around intelligent systems.
entries.subject: AI-native universities
entries.author: Emily Bennett

entries.label: Building the AI-native industrial base
entries.quote: Energy, manufacturing, logistics, and infrastructure are back in focus, and the most important shift is the rise of an industrial base that is truly AI native and software-first.
entries.subject: AI-native industrial base
entries.author: David Ulevitch

entries.label: The renaissance of the American factory
entries.quote: In 2026, I think we’ll see companies approach challenges spanning energy, mining, construction, and manufacturing with a factory mindset.
entries.subject: Factory-style production in heavy industry
entries.author: Erin Price-Wright

entries.label: The next wave of observability will be physical, not digital
entries.quote: The same revolution is coming to the physical world.
entries.subject: Physical-world observability
entries.author: Zabie Elmgren

entries.label: The electro-industrial stack will move the world
entries.quote: The nations that master the electro-industrial stack will define the future of industrial and military technologies.
entries.subject: Electro-industrial stack (electrification hardware)
entries.author: Ryan McEntush

entries.label: Autonomous labs accelerate scientific discovery
entries.quote: As model capabilities progress across modalities and robotic manipulation capabilities continue to improve, teams will accelerate their pursuit of autonomous scientific discovery.
entries.subject: Autonomous science labs
entries.author: Oliver Hsu

entries.label: Data crusade in our critical industries
entries.quote: In 2026, it will be defined by data constraints and the next frontier in the crusade for data: our critical industries.
entries.subject: Data collection in critical industries
entries.author: Will Bitsky

entries.label: AI reinforces business models
entries.quote: In 2026, we’ll see this logic extend across industries, as AI systems deepen alignment with their customers’ incentives and create compounding advantages legacy software can’t touch.
entries.subject: AI aligned with customer business models
entries.author: David Haber

entries.label: ChatGPT becomes the AI app store
entries.quote: As the final piece in the consumer product cycle, this new distribution channel is set to kick off a once-in-a-decade gold rush in consumer tech in 2026.
entries.subject: ChatGPT as an app distribution platform
entries.author: Anish Acharya

entries.label: Voice agents take up space
entries.quote: I’m excited to see voice agents expand into handling entire workflows (which might be multi-modal) and even into managing full customer relationship cycles.
entries.subject: AI voice agents for business
entries.author: Olivia Moore

entries.label: Prompt-free and proactive applications arrive
entries.quote: 2026 marks the death of the prompt box for mainstream users.
entries.subject: Proactive (prompt-free) AI applications
entries.author: Marc Andrusko

entries.label: AI will finally upgrade banking and insurance infrastructure
entries.quote: In 2026, the risk of not modernizing to take full advantage of AI will outweigh the risk of failure, and we’ll see large financial institutions let their legacy vendor contracts lapse and start implementing newer, AI-native alternatives.
entries.subject: AI-native core systems in banking and insurance
entries.author: Angela Strange

entries.label: Forward-deployed motions take AI to the 99%
entries.quote: Companies will realize that the vast majority of the AI opportunity lives outside of Silicon Valley, and we’re going to see new founders use forward-deployed motions to discover more opportunities that are hiding inside big, legacy verticals.
entries.subject: Forward-deployed AI adoption in legacy industries
entries.author: Joe Schmidt

entries.label: AI creates a new orchestration layer—and new roles—in the Fortune 500
entries.quote: In 2026, enterprises will shift further from isolated AI tools to multi-agent systems that will need to behave like coordinated digital teams.
entries.subject: Multi-agent orchestration in enterprises
entries.author: Seema Amble

entries.label: Consumer AI shifts from “help me” to “see me”
entries.quote: 2026 marks the year major consumer AI products shift from productivity to connectivity.
entries.subject: Consumer AI for social connection
entries.author: Bryan Kim

entries.label: New model primitives unlock previously impossible companies
entries.quote: In 2026, we’ll see the emergence of companies that simply could not have existed before recent model breakthroughs in reasoning, multimodality, and computer use.
entries.subject: Companies enabled by new model capabilities
entries.author: Kimberly Tan

entries.label: AI startups selling to other AI startups reach scale
entries.quote: 2026 will be the year that we see the startups going greenfield reach scale across a host of enterprise software categories.
entries.subject: AI startups as customers of AI startups
entries.author: James da Costa

entries.label: Privacy will be the most important moat in crypto
entries.quote: But now, privacy by itself is sufficiently compelling to differentiate a chain from all the rest.
entries.subject: Privacy-preserving blockchains
entries.author: Ali Yahya

entries.label: Prediction markets go bigger, broader, and smarter
entries.quote: Prediction markets have already gone mainstream, and this coming year, they’ll only become bigger, broader, and smarter as they intersect with crypto and AI — while also posing new and important challenges for builders to resolve.
entries.subject: Prediction markets
entries.author: Andrew Hall

entries.label: Thinking about tokenization of real world assets, and stablecoins, in a more crypto-native way
entries.quote: Along similar lines, in 2026 we’ll see more “origination, not just tokenization” when it comes to stablecoins, which went mainstream in 2025; outstanding stablecoin issuance continues to grow.
entries.subject: Crypto-native asset origination and stablecoins
entries.author: Guy Wuollet

entries.label: Trading as a way station, not the last stop, for crypto businesses
entries.quote: The founders who focus on the “product” part of product-market fit may end up the bigger winners.
entries.subject: Crypto company business models beyond trading
entries.author: Arianna Simpson

entries.label: From know your customer (KYC) to ‘know your agent’ (KYA)
entries.quote: Just as humans need credit scores to get loans, agents will need cryptographically signed credentials to transact — linking the agent to its principal, its constraints, and its liability.
entries.subject: Know your agent (KYA) credentials for AI agents
entries.author: Sean Neville
entries.note: Guest contributor, not a16z staff (bio on the page: cofounder of Circle; CEO of Catena Labs). Part 3 says it includes 'a few guest contributors'.

entries.label: Better, more clever onramps/ offramps for stablecoins
entries.quote: As these on/off ramps mature, with digital dollars plugging directly into local payment systems and merchant tools, new behaviors will emerge: Workers can be paid in real time across borders.
entries.subject: Stablecoin on/off ramps
entries.author: Jeremy Zhang
entries.note: Text states stablecoins handled an estimated 46 trillion dollars in transaction volume 'last year' (current, not a forecast).

entries.label: Stablecoins unlock the bank ledger upgrade cycle — and new payment scenarios
entries.quote: That’s where stablecoins come in.
entries.subject: Stablecoins and bank core ledger modernization
entries.author: Sam Broner

entries.label: The (near) future of messaging isn’t just quantum-resistant. It’s decentralized
entries.quote: Messaging needs open protocols where we don’t have to trust anyone.
entries.subject: Decentralized quantum-resistant messaging
entries.author: Shane Mac
entries.note: Guest contributor, not a16z staff (bio on the page: co-founder and CEO, XMTP Labs). Part 3 says it includes 'a few guest contributors'.

entries.label: From ‘code is law’ to ‘spec is law’
entries.quote: To mature, DeFi security needs to move from bug patterns to design-level properties, and from “best-effort” to “principled” approaches:
entries.subject: Formal specification and runtime enforcement in DeFi security
entries.author: Daejun Park

entries.label: Crypto offers a new primitive for use beyond blockchains
entries.quote: In 2026, zkVM provers will hit roughly 10,000X overhead with memory footprints in the hundreds of megabytes — fast enough to run on phones, cheap enough to run everywhere.
entries.subject: zkVM provers (verifiable computation)
entries.author: Justin Thaler
entries.note: Same quote states memory footprints in the hundreds of megabytes.

entries.label: We’ll use AI for substantive research tasks
entries.quote: But I’m expecting AI research to enable, and reward, a new type of polymath research style: one that favors an ability to conjecture relationships between ideas, and quickly extrapolate from even more conjectural answers.
entries.subject: AI for research
entries.author: Scott Duke Kominers

entries.label: The invisible tax on the open web
entries.quote: The key transition for the coming year will be moving from static licensing to real-time, usage-based compensation.
entries.subject: Usage-based compensation for web content used by AI
entries.author: Elizabeth Harkavy

entries.label: The rise of staked media
entries.quote: Tokenized assets, programmable lockups, prediction markets, and onchain histories offer stronger foundations for trust: A commentator can publish an argument and also prove they’re putting their money where their mouth is.
entries.subject: Staked media (cryptographically verifiable commitments)
entries.author: Robert Hackett

entries.label: ‘Secrets-as-a-service’
entries.quote: That’s why I believe we need secrets-as-a-service: New technologies that can provide programmable, native data access rules; client-side encryption; and decentralized key management enforcing who can decrypt what, under which conditions, and for how long… all enforced onchain.
entries.subject: Programmable data access control (secrets-as-a-service)
entries.author: Adeniyi Abiodun
entries.note: Guest contributor, not a16z staff (bio on the page: chief product officer and co-founder, Mysten Labs). Part 3 says it includes 'a few guest contributors'.

entries.label: Wealth management for all
entries.quote: But as more asset classes are tokenized, crypto rails enable strategies — personalized with AI recommendations and co-pilots – to be executed and rebalanced instantly and with minimal cost.
entries.subject: Tokenized personalized wealth management
entries.author: Maggie Hsu

entries.label: The internet becomes the bank
entries.quote: But in 2026, emerging primitives like x402 make that settlement programmable and reactive.
entries.subject: Programmable internet-native payments (x402)
entries.author: Christian Crowley

entries.label: Unleashing the full potential of blockchains… when legal architecture finally matches technical architecture
entries.quote: But crypto market structure regulation — which the government is closer to passing than it’s ever been — has the potential to eliminate all of these distortions next year.
entries.subject: US crypto market structure legislation
entries.author: Miles Jennings
